clue.text: Article about enclosed space, the cosmological matter for discussion

indicators.note: about means going round, so the newspaper piece wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a newspaper article is a story
a ring is an enclosed space, as for boxing or a circus
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a confined area turns out to be a cosmic topic for debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' tempts as A or THE, but here it is a newspaper piece; 'about' wraps it round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: String theory is a speculative physical model of the universe, still a matter for scientific discussion rather than settled fact.

clue.text: One going in to join fighter

indicators.note: going in signals that one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to solder is to join metals with molten alloy
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone entering to sign up with a combatant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One going in' reads like a recruit enlisting, but 'going in' is the container signal; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is a member of an army, someone who fights.

clue.text: Butler, bisexual holy man

parts.note: RAB Butler was a senior British Conservative politician of the mid-twentieth century

explanation.surface: A servant named Butler who is bisexual and also a man of God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butler' looks like a servant but is the politician R. A. Butler, always known as RAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher, a holy man of that faith.

clue.text: Poor Paul in trouble without money, seeking marriage

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order
without means the money is taken away from the word trouble

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian unit of money

explanation.surface: Poor penniless Paul, in difficulties, is looking for a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble without money' is TROUBLE with ROUBLE removed, leaving T; 'Poor' then rearranges PAULIN + T.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial means relating to marriage or a wedding, so an adjective fitting someone in search of a spouse.

clue.text: Problem ending pain with basis of plaster

indicators.note: ending tells us the problem word comes at the end, after the pain word

parts.note: gyp is British slang for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A difficulty that brings an ache to an end, combined with the base of plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word. GYP is informal British for pain or discomfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum is the mineral calcium sulphate, the raw material from which plaster of Paris is made.

clue.text: Frivolous introduction to Beverley, East Yorkshire

indicators.note: the run straddles the town's last letter, the compass word and the opening of the county, introducing Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A light-hearted guide to the Yorkshire market town of Beverley.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across beverleY EAST Yorkshire. Beverley is a town in the East Riding of Yorkshire, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeasty can mean frothy, so figuratively light and frivolous, like a fizzing ferment.

clue.text: Very difficult answer coming up as instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: murder is informal for something very hard, as in 'parking here is murder'

explanation.surface: A tough response arising in the form of a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns MURDER + ANS to give the whole answer; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument with wires stretched across its lower head.

clue.text: Time when confidence lacking if (might one say) credit is doubled

parts.note: the little word if sits in the very middle of the word life, so it might be called mid-life
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: doubled means the word is should appear twice in a row

explanation.surface: A period of self-doubt arrives when one's borrowing power has doubled.
explanation.walkthrough: The '(might one say)' flags a whimsical description: IF stands in the middle of LIFE. Then CR + IS + IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A midlife crisis is a period of anxiety and lost self-assurance some people go through in middle age.

clue.text: My topic called complex — in just that manner?

indicators.note: complex suggests something intricate and tangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has made their chosen subject intricate, and the clue asks if that is the way it is done.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the fact that the anagram itself has been made in a complicated way.
explanation.definitionFit: Complicatedly means in a complex or involved way, which is how the clue's letters have been treated.

clue.text: Cry when onion's brought round

indicators.note: brought round means one letter is shifted to another spot in the word

parts.note: an onion is a bulb

explanation.surface: Weeping when an onion is fetched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link. Moving the L of BULB forward gives B-L-U-B.
explanation.definitionFit: To blub is a British informal word for to cry or sob.

clue.text: Brainwashing has genuine look if pronounced

indicators.note: if pronounced signals that the words are said out loud and heard as something else

parts.note: proper means genuine and a gander is a look, so the two together are proper gander

explanation.surface: Indoctrination seems authentic when said aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link. 'Have a gander' is British slang for take a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is biased information spread to shape opinion, a form of mass brainwashing.

clue.text: State with little resort on the Adriatic

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island
mini means small

explanation.surface: A country together with a small holiday town on the Adriatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is an Italian seaside town on the Adriatic coast, famous for its beaches.

clue.text: Miserable old news people given endless credit

parts.note: Pathe News made cinema newsreels in Britain for much of the twentieth century

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: An unhappy former newsreel company that is allowed unlimited borrowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips the last letter from TICK, leaving TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic means pitifully inadequate, so miserable in the sense of wretched or poor.

clue.text: A fan with girls excited, as tongues entwining?

indicators.note: excited suggests agitation, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An eager admirer surrounded by girls, perhaps kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two fodder pieces and gives no letters; 'as' is a link. The question mark flags the playful picture of languages kissing.
explanation.definitionFit: Franglais is French mixed with English words, a blending of two languages.

clue.text: Architect left in repulsive US city

parts.note: John Nash designed Regency London, including Regent Street

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the word for repulsive

parts.note: vile means repulsive

explanation.surface: A designer has left a disgusting American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville is the capital of Tennessee, famous for country music.

clue.text: Second-rate wine? Sling away for cheese

parts.note: B is the second grade, so second-rate

indicators.note: away means the named word is removed from the grape wine

parts.note: Riesling is a white wine grape and wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mediocre wine is thrown out in favour of some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sling' looks like a verb meaning throw, but is the letters taken from RIESLING, leaving RIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese with a white rind.

clue.text: Pound Shop — not for her!

indicators.note: to pound is to batter, so the following word is beaten into a new shape

explanation.surface: A cheap discount store is beneath a certain kind of lady.
explanation.walkthrough: A pound shop sells everything for one pound; 'Pound' is the anagram signal, and the whole clue describes the upper-class woman who would shun such a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A posh person, smart and upper-class, would never be seen shopping at a bargain store.

clue.text: Carry on forward to embrace female relation

indicators.note: to embrace means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: forward can mean cheeky, which is pert
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: Keep going ahead and hug a sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' is not a direction but an adjective meaning cheeky, PERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to carry on doing something in spite of difficulty.

clue.text: Reserve I show behind world leader

parts.note: a bank is a reserve or store
to moon is to expose one's backside

explanation.surface: Backup arrives as I bare my bottom behind a global figure.
explanation.walkthrough: BAN KI-MOON was Secretary-General of the United Nations, 2007 to 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: As UN Secretary-General he headed the world's chief international organisation.

clue.text: Stone breaker last to crack nut

indicators.note: last to picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: nut and napper are both slang for the head

explanation.surface: A stone-cutter is the final person to split a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' looks like the thing being cracked but is slang for the head, NAPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A knapper shapes or breaks stone, especially flint, by striking it.

clue.text: Real SOS put out, as stranded on the water?

indicators.note: put out suggests something disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A genuine distress call sent out by someone marooned at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link. The definition is playful: a rower with no oars is stuck on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Being oarless means having no oars, which would leave a boat helplessly stranded.

clue.text: Upside-down pot, container

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside-down means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a pot is a prize fund, so a reward

explanation.surface: An overturned pot used as a receptacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawer is a sliding box in a piece of furniture, used to contain things.

clue.text: Partygoers given drug after little time, getting 23

indicators.note: after says the partygoers and drug come behind the short time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
ravers are people who go to raves
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Clubbers take ecstasy shortly and get angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' and 'getting' are links. The definition is the answer to 23, CROSS, in its sense of going over.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross a place is to go over it from one side to the other, the meaning of traverse.

clue.text: Agreement, something struck out loud?

indicators.note: out loud means the words are spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: a chord is struck on a piano or guitar

explanation.surface: A deal reached, something hit noisily?
explanation.definitionFit: An accord is a formal agreement, such as one between nations.

clue.text: Bridge put out

definitions.meaning: to bridge something is to span it or go over it
put out means annoyed or irritated

explanation.surface: A bridge has been put out of action.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross is to go over something, as a bridge does, and cross also means angry or irritated.

clue.text: Linen item with facing edges carrying blue stripe, firstly

indicators.note: carrying means the outer pair hold the other letters inside them

parts.note: edges are lips, and two facing each other read one backwards and one forwards
edges are lips, and two facing each other read one backwards and one forwards
blue means sad or low

indicators.note: firstly takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A piece of linen whose opposite borders bear a blue stripe.
explanation.walkthrough: Two edges facing each other are a pair of lips mirrored, one read backwards; 'carrying' puts the middle pieces between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillowslip is a cotton or linen cover for a pillow, part of the household linen.

clue.text: Dog without lead, finished

indicators.note: without lead means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Rover is a traditional name for a dog

explanation.surface: A dog let off its leash is all done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a dog's leash but is the leading letter of ROVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means ended, as in 'the game is over'.
